sections.title: Admin: Acme Console
sections.description: Acme Console, the back-office where Acme staff set up client companies, groups, client users, SLA policies and SSO.
rules: A "user" here is a client end user (an agent of a client company), never a colleague: giving a colleague access is internal-tools/accounts.
When the question is about what can be chosen on a group, also open the company settings (parent level).
What a company can allow is itself capped by its plan: also open product/plans-and-features.
Setting up a new client: the runbook gives the order, the screen docs give the fields, sales/account-roles-and-handover gives who does what.

sections.title: Internal tools: Acme Hub and Acme Billing
sections.description: Acme Hub (pipeline, client health, reports) and Acme Billing (billing accounts, invoices, credit notes): access and daily use.
rules: A "user" or an "account" in Acme Hub is an Acme employee using the tool, never a client.
In Acme Billing, a "billing account" is the billing record of a client company; a colleague with access is a "member".
Reports here are internal figures about Acme, never the reports clients see in Acme Desk.

sections.title: Legal & security
sections.description: GDPR roles, DPAs, subprocessors, certifications, security rules for employees, security incidents, data subject requests.
rules: For an answer given to a client, these pages are the reference; sales/security-questionnaire gives the ready-made wording.
A security incident (data or access at risk) is handled here; an outage or a broken feature is support-ops.

sections.title: People & HR
sections.description: HR policies for Acme employees, with no personal data: leave, remote work, expenses, travel, equipment, first week.
rules: If a topic is not documented here, say so and point to people/hr-contacts. Never answer HR questions from general knowledge.

sections.title: Product: Acme Desk
sections.description: How the client-facing helpdesk app works: plans, roles, channels, SLAs, inbox, reports, login, API, data retention and export.
rules: A "user" in this section is an agent or supervisor of a client working in Acme Desk, never an Acme employee.
The channels a client group can use are capped by the channels allowed for its company: also open admin/companies.
An SLA here is a target a client sets for its own customers, never the uptime commitment of Acme (support-ops/uptime-commitment).

sections.title: Sales
sections.description: Pricing, sales process, trials, proposals, renewals, who does what on an account, answers to security questionnaires.
rules: A price marked to_confirm must be presented as not confirmed yet.
For data retention or security answers given to a client, product/data-retention is the reference page.
An "account plan" is a sales document about a client; a "plan" alone is an Acme Desk subscription plan.

sections.title: Support operations
sections.description: How Acme's own support team works: levels, escalation, on-call, incidents, uptime commitment, refunds and credits.
rules: These pages describe the support Acme gives its clients, not the helpdesk features of Acme Desk.
Support hours, response targets and the uptime commitment here are Acme's own, never the settings of a client group.
